questions.question: You see pedestrians near the road. What should you do?

options.text: Honk your horn and keep your speed.
Speed up to get past them quickly.

questions.explanation: Watch for pedestrians who might cross into your path. If you see pedestrians near the road, slow down and be ready to stop if needed.

questions.question: As your blood alcohol level (BAC) increases, you become:
questions.explanation: Blood alcohol concentration (BAC) measures how much alcohol is in your blood. The higher your BAC, the more impaired you are.

questions.question: Before changing lanes or passing another vehicle, you should:

options.text: Check your blind spots and mirrors.
Signal to show other drivers what you plan to do.

questions.explanation: Always signal before changing lanes to alert other drivers. Check your mirrors and look over your shoulder to check your blind spot before moving left or right.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. They alert you to road hazards ahead. This sign warns you that traffic is merging from the right. Be ready to let them merge safely.

questions.question: If another driver cuts you off, what should you do?

options.text: Pull up next to the driver and yell at them.
Flash your high beams at the driver.
Cut them off to get back at them.

questions.explanation: Do not take it personally if another driver cuts you off. Let it go and keep driving safely. This helps prevent road rage and accidents.

questions.question: When an emergency vehicle with sirens and flashing lights approaches you, you must pull to the right side of the road and wait for it to pass.
questions.explanation: When you see or hear an emergency vehicle using lights and sirens, pull to the right side of the road immediately and stop to let it pass.

questions.question: What can happen when you mix alcohol with another drug?

options.text: The effects of both may become stronger.
The effects of both may become weaker.
Only the alcohol's effects may become weaker.

questions.correctAnswerText: The effects of both may become stronger.
questions.explanation: Mixing alcohol with another drug can make both effects stronger. For example, one drink while taking a cold medicine can affect you like having several drinks.

questions.question: You must stop at a railroad crossing when:

options.text: A flagger directs you to stop.
Flashing red lights and gates are active.

questions.explanation: Stop at railroad crossings when a flagger or stop sign tells you to. Also stop when flashing red lights and gates are working.

questions.question: You hear a siren behind you. What should you do?

options.text: Pull over to the right and stop.
Speed up to get out of the way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over to the right and stop.
questions.explanation: When you hear a siren or see flashing lights behind you, pull to the right side of the road and stop. Create a clear path for the emergency vehicle. If you are in heavy traffic, move slowly to the side when you can.

questions.question: What does a "No standing" sign mean?

options.text: You can never stop your vehicle there.
You can park there if you stay in the vehicle.
You can stop briefly only to pick up or drop off passengers.
You can stop to load or unload goods.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can stop briefly only to pick up or drop off passengers.
questions.explanation: A "No standing" sign means you can only make a brief stop to load or unload passengers.

questions.question: If your vehicle has a two-part safety belt system, what should you do?

options.text: Use both the lap and shoulder belts.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the lap and shoulder belts.
questions.explanation: Always wear both the lap belt and the shoulder belt. Using only one part does not protect you as well. Even if you have an automatic shoulder belt, you must also buckle your lap belt.

questions.question: Like alcohol and other drugs, drowsiness can:

options.text: Help you be a better driver.

questions.explanation: Not getting enough sleep causes poor driving. Drowsiness slows your reaction time, reduces awareness, and impairs judgment — just like alcohol and drugs.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, you should wait until the entire car is visible in your rearview mirror before moving back into the right lane.
questions.explanation: When passing, do not return to your original lane until you can see the entire vehicle you passed in your rearview mirror.

questions.question: On a long trip, what can help prevent fatigue?

options.text: Stop and rest every two hours.
Drive with one eye open at a time.
Change feet on the gas pedal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and rest every two hours.
questions.explanation: Take a break every two hours on long trips. If you feel drowsy, pull over safely and nap or stay overnight.

questions.question: The maximum posted speed limit should only be driven:
questions.explanation: The posted speed limit is the fastest you can legally drive when conditions are perfect. Drive at the same speed as other traffic, up to the limit. All drivers must drive safely at all times.

questions.question: To avoid becoming an aggressive driver, you should:

options.text: Drive above the posted speed limit.
Tailgate the driver in front of you.

questions.explanation: Focus on driving and do not take other drivers' actions personally. Plan extra travel time, follow speed limits, and be patient with other drivers.

questions.question: Pedestrians in crosswalks and at intersections always have the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: Pedestrians have the right-of-way at intersections. A crosswalk exists at any intersection, whether it is marked or not.

questions.question: In which ways can alcohol affect you?
questions.explanation: Alcohol weakens the brain's control over judgment and self-control. You may feel overly confident. Alcohol also slows reaction time, reduces coordination, and weakens your vision and ability to judge distance.

questions.question: Tailgating other drivers (driving too close to their rear bumper):

options.text: Can frustrate other drivers and make them angry.
Cannot result in a traffic citation.
Prevents collisions by stopping being cut off.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can frustrate other drivers and make them angry.
questions.explanation: Tailgating is a dangerous behavior that can lead to aggressive driving. You can face legal penalties for unsafe driving.

questions.question: You may leave the scene of a collision if the damage does not look serious.
questions.explanation: Never leave the scene of a collision. If you do, you may be charged with a hit and run.
